title: Frontier Systems Compendium
summary: Publish eight source-bound lane chapters and four cross-system essays while preserving all twenty-four official artifacts and seventy-two claim blocks exactly once in the chapter layer.
record_scope: Append-only Phase 165–172 evidence-to-publication overlay over immutable Phase 156 and Phase 164 validation receipts.
publication_boundaries: This is an append-only operating and content layer over the immutable Phase 156 and Phase 164 receipts; it does not rewrite either validated baseline.
Only evidence checks lawful on or before 2026-09-01 may carry a decision. Later September and October outcomes remain null until their recorded dates.

Candidate sources, planned capacity, service availability, offers, forecasts, and adjacent facts do not substitute for the exact observation, authority, period, method, and denominator required by a gate.
No owner decision, project or place stage, admitted longitudinal series, causal result, score, rank, repository publication, hosted deployment, or v1 promotion is inferred.

claim_blocks.text: NERC reports that assessment-area summer peak demand is forecast to rise by more than 224 GW from 2025 through 2035 and winter peak demand by about 245 GW. The assessment attributes most projected growth to data centers and distinguishes 71 GW of approved summer-capacity growth from 266 GW of prospective additions.
claim_blocks.publication_state: Published context — not an evidence-admission decision

claim_blocks.text: The artifact supplies a bounded planner forecast and adequacy assessment for the Power and grid evidence chain. It can orient the named topics and linked project or place files only at the entity, period, measure, and authority scope stated by the issuer.
The figures are forecasts assembled from mid-2025 planner submissions. They are not observed load, proof that each data-center proposal will connect, or proof of a future capacity shortfall.

Berkeley Lab identifies about 8,200 active projects representing 1,312 GW of generation and 749 GW of storage at the end of 2025. About 549 GW had a draft or executed interconnection agreement without commercial operation, and the median request-to-operation time exceeded five years for projects completed in 2025.

claim_blocks.text: The artifact supplies a bounded official laboratory queue dataset and report for the Power and grid evidence chain. It can orient the named topics and linked project or place files only at the entity, period, measure, and authority scope stated by the issuer.

Queue records cover transmission-level requests and exclude distribution and behind-the-meter projects. A queue entry or interconnection agreement is not a completed plant, an operating observation, or a forecast.

EIA reports 43.6 GW of operational utility-scale battery nameplate capacity at year-end 2025 and another 8.3 GW added in the first half of 2026, bringing the total near 52 GW. The release identifies Manatee as 409 MW of battery capacity paired with 75 MW of solar capacity.

compendium_records.title: Compute demand, grid queues, and water constraints
compendium_records.thesis: Large-load demand can be announced faster than interconnection, generation, water, and local approvals become accepted service. The useful comparison is a dependency chain, not a single capacity total.
compendium_records.synthesis: Large-load demand can be announced faster than interconnection, generation, water, and local approvals become accepted service. The useful comparison is a dependency chain, not a single capacity total. The editorial task is to show the sequence of claims a reader would need to verify: first the authoritative baseline, then the named intervention, then accepted delivery, then recurring operation, and finally an outcome measured for a stable population or asset denominator. Evidence can stop at any link. A missing link remains visible rather than being estimated from a neighboring system.
decision_questions: Which entity and authority own the measure?
What date and data-through period apply?
Is the measure planned, installed, accepted, recurring, or observed?
What denominator and revision lineage make comparison lawful?
Which distributional or local-system effects remain outside the artifact?
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not convert a forecast into observed demand.
Do not convert an award into accepted capacity.
Do not transfer one jurisdiction’s denominator to another.
Do not infer causal benefit from temporal sequence or co-location.
Do not score systems whose evidence types are incompatible.
compendium_records.boundary: The essay synthesizes already published packet claims and creates no new source check, admission decision, comparison verdict, score, or rank.

compendium_records.title: Announcement-to-accepted-capacity conversion
compendium_records.thesis: Capital announcements, awards, construction milestones, qualification, and accepted recurring capacity answer different questions. This essay supplies a common conversion grammar without forcing unlike systems into one stage.
compendium_records.synthesis: Capital announcements, awards, construction milestones, qualification, and accepted recurring capacity answer different questions. This essay supplies a common conversion grammar without forcing unlike systems into one stage. The editorial task is to show the sequence of claims a reader would need to verify: first the authoritative baseline, then the named intervention, then accepted delivery, then recurring operation, and finally an outcome measured for a stable population or asset denominator. Evidence can stop at any link. A missing link remains visible rather than being estimated from a neighboring system.
decision_questions: Which entity and authority own the measure?
What date and data-through period apply?
Is the measure planned, installed, accepted, recurring, or observed?
What denominator and revision lineage make comparison lawful?
Which distributional or local-system effects remain outside the artifact?
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not convert a forecast into observed demand.
Do not convert an award into accepted capacity.
Do not transfer one jurisdiction’s denominator to another.
Do not infer causal benefit from temporal sequence or co-location.
Do not score systems whose evidence types are incompatible.
compendium_records.boundary: The essay synthesizes already published packet claims and creates no new source check, admission decision, comparison verdict, score, or rank.

compendium_records.title: Infrastructure delivery versus observed public outcomes
